summary: Keyword co-occurrence in Baileys media utility; no traced installer harm
details: zero-baileys@3.4.6 is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. The static match cites lib/Utils/messages-media.js where require('child_process'), https.request, a hostname reference, and a POST verb co-occur in a media-handling utility. This co-occurrence is the shared shape of media transcoding (spawning ffmpeg) and normal HTTPS uploads/downloads to caller-configured WhatsApp media hosts; the rule cannot distinguish it from exfiltration. No specific installer-side secret is named as being read, no non-first-party destination is identified, and no install-time or import-time execution of this code path is shown. Baileys forks have historically included covert side-effects such as auto-following an author-controlled newsletter channel using the caller's session, which would be a separate concern from this particular file, but is not evidenced here.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
